confirmed.description: The Portuguese brand on Nagoji's bared LEFT forearm is drawn just below the elbow, right under the pushed-back sleeve. The bible puts it a hand's width above the wrist, a position the author locked. The brand also moves between three panels in a row: mid-forearm with the white scar cutting across it in 14.1, up near the elbow in 14.2, and near the wrist in 15.1 and 15.2, which are correct. In 14.2 the RIGHT sleeve is also rolled above the elbow, but the bible pushes back only the left sleeve.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of the bottom of 14.2: the raised ridged patch sits on the upper forearm, directly below the rolled cream sleeve, and the viewer-left forearm is bare with its sleeve rolled too. In 14.1 the ridged patch is about halfway between wrist and elbow. In 15.1 and 15.2 it is about one hand above the wrist, with the scar running alongside it.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. The problem shows on the page.

Page 14, panel 2 (from a 4x crop of the bottom edge): Nagoji's left forearm is on the viewer's right. Its sleeve is rolled to the elbow. A pale, lumpy, ridged patch sits just below the sleeve cuff, in the upper third of the forearm. A faint thin pale line, the scar, runs down beside it. The panel cuts off at sash level, so the wrist is out of frame. That puts the brand near the elbow, not a hand's width above the wrist. CONTINUITY.md row "9 @14-" sets that position, and the script says the author locked it on 2026-09-26.

The brand also jumps between neighbouring panels:
- 14.1: about halfway between wrist and elbow, with the white scar crossing over it rather than running alongside.
- 14.2: just below the elbow.
- 15.1 and 15.2: near the wrist, as the script asks.
The script makes this arm the subject of pages 14 and 15. At 300 DPI the patch in 14.2 prints at about 0.15 x 0.22 inch, pale on brown skin. That is small but easy to see, so it matters at print size.

The sleeve point also holds. The script says his sleeves stay down except where "the left sleeve is pushed back", and the "9 @14-" row pushes back only the left one. In 14.1 his right sleeve correctly reaches the wrist. In 14.2 the right sleeve is rolled above the elbow and the forearm is bare. That is a costume change between consecutive panels. 15.1 repeats the same rolled right sleeve, so that panel needs the same fix.

Severity is major rather than blocker. Nagoji is still clearly himself, and the fix is local: paint over or regenerate the lower forearm in 14.2 so the brand is out of frame or near the wrist, and roll the right sleeve down.

confirmed.description: The brand on Nagoji's bared LEFT forearm sits just below the elbow crease instead of a hand's width above the wrist. The bible row for 9 @14- and the 2026-09-26 author lock both fix it near the wrist. It also contradicts 14.1 (mid-forearm) and 15.1/15.2 (just above the wrist), so the brand moves three times across consecutive panels.
confirmed.evidence: page-14.png, lower panel, Nagoji's left arm at frame right: a pale puckered ridged patch directly under the rolled sleeve at the elbow (about x 1000-1060, y 2290-2400 at full resolution), with the forearm continuing out of frame below it. Compare 15.1, where the same patch sits about two finger-widths above the wrist.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page-14.png, panel 14.2. I cropped it at full resolution (x 300-1150, y 1780-2560). Nagoji's bared left arm at frame right has the brand's pale, puckered, ridged patch at about x 950-990, y 2415-2480. That is directly under the rolled sleeve, which meets the arm at about y 2360-2400. To place it on the arm, I used his head as a ruler (crown about y 1835, chin about y 2035) to estimate where the wrist falls. Shoulder to elbow runs about y 2110 to 2385, so the forearm should be about 210-230 px long and the wrist should sit at about y 2600, below the frame edge at about y 2540. That puts the patch in the top third of the forearm, near the elbow. CONTINUITY row "9 @14-" and the script's standing note (inner left forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, locked by the author on 2026-09-26) put it about a third of the forearm up from the wrist, which here is at or just below the panel's bottom edge. Nothing in the 14.2 script text permits a different spot. The patch is about 4 x 5.5 mm at print size and reads clearly as a pale ridged mark against the warm skin, so it is not too slight to see. Pages 14 and 15 also print as facing pages (88/89). On page 15, panels 15.1 and 15.2 make the brand the subject of the panel and draw it just above the wrist, so a reader sees the brand jump from near the elbow to the wrist across the spread. Panel 14.1 is also high (about mid-forearm), so the reviewer is right that the brand moves between panels. This is a localized continuity error that breaks an author-locked identity mark, not a missing beat, so major rather than blocker. The fix is small: the correct position falls at or past the frame edge, so painting the patch out of 14.2 would make it agree with the bible and with page 15. No files were edited. This review does not approve or apply the separate CONTINUITY change mentioned in the relayed request; that is for the author to approve.

confirmed.description: Revathi's necklace is drawn as round gold beads, not the flat-coin necklace the bible and script require. This panel's beat is 'her fingers closing briefly on the coins at her throat', so the prop the action depends on is wrong. The necklace changes from panel to panel through the chapter: flat coin discs in 4.1, 4.3, 5.2, 6.2, 7.3, 12.1 and 15.1, round beads in 4.2, 5.1, 7.5, 8.3, 10.1, 10.3, 12.3 and 14.1.
confirmed.evidence: page-10.png top panel: her fingertips rest on a row of spherical gold beads (crop around x 460-860, y 530-810). page-06.png 6.2, by contrast, shows flat embossed coin discs.

verdict.reason:
The finding is accurate, but it isn't major.

What the art shows: on page 10, panel 10.1, her fingertips rest on a row of round, shiny gold beads, clearly visible at full zoom. Panel 10.3 shows the same beads. Panel 6.2 shows flat, embossed coin discs. The base line for Revathi in CONTINUITY.md calls for a "flat-coin necklace", and the script calls for "a necklace of flat gold coins" and "the coins at her throat" in 10.1. So the panel breaks the written spec, and the chapter switches between discs and beads. That is real, so I can't refute it.

Why it is minor:
- 10.1 matches the approved Revathi sheet (concepts/05-revathi-bayi-v15f.png). That sheet draws round gold beads in the 3/4 view and in all six expression heads. The panel is following its approved reference. The real conflict is between the sheet and the bible text, not a mistake local to 10.1.
- Redrawing 10.1 alone would not fix the switching across the chapter. The author has to choose coins or beads, then fix the sheet or the bible to match and apply it across the chapter. Under the author's own rule, a CONTINUITY change needs their approval.
- The beat still works. Her hand closes on the gold necklace at her throat, and no lettering mentions coins. A reader would only notice by comparing the 6.2 close-up with 10.1 four pages later.

Separately: I gave no approval for the CONTINUITY change mentioned in the relayed request. That approval has to come from the author, and nothing in this review grants it.

confirmed.description: Padmini's horse changes colour between pages. On page 1 she rides a bay (red-brown coat, black mane). At the gate in 2.1 the same horse is near-black with a white blaze. It is the same ride and the next panel.
confirmed.evidence: page-01.png 1.3: the horse at frame left under Padmini is a red-brown bay with a black mane, and 1.2 also shows her on a brown bay. page-02.png 2.1: the horse under Padmini (centre, behind the balloon) has a black coat with a white blaze down the face.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In page-02.png panel 2.1, Padmini's reins lead to a horse whose neck, mane and head sit directly in front of her hands. That horse is near-black: the neck samples at about RGB (44,38,33), the mane is black, and a sharp white blaze runs down the face. On page 1 the same ride shows her horse as a warm red-brown bay with a black mane. The 1.3 face samples at about RGB (81,55,37), and the bay at the right edge of 1.4 has a small white facial mark. Page 1.2 also shows her on a brown bay. Both scenes are in full daylight, so lighting does not explain it. 2.1 is the very next beat, after the page turn from 75 to 76. The script calls it "a compact horse", and neither the script nor CONTINUITY.md sets a coat colour for Padmini's horse. The only bible horse rule here is Kayal (Nagoji's bay, no white markings), and Nagoji's horse in 2.1 matches it. So nothing permits a change mid-ride, and the coat simply switches from bay to black between consecutive panels. The black head and white blaze are plainly visible above the balloon at print size, not a slight shade difference. The fix is local: repaint or redraw Padmini's mount in 2.1 as the page-1 bay. This is not a blocker because her identity, the lettering and the beat are all correct; it is a localized continuity error like a costume slip, so major. (Panel 2.2 shows only a dark saddle edge as she dismounts and needs no separate fix.)

confirmed.description: The callback boots in the insert are a different pair. Here they are tall, knee-high slouch boots with a single tie, standing on the flat floor. In 3.1, the 13.3 inset and 14.1 (and on the commander sheet) they are mid-calf boots with crossing wrap straps set on the verandah step. The boots are the whole subject of the panel ('your feet are already on the path'), so the mismatch reads as a different object.
confirmed.evidence: page-11.png top right panel: tall boots reaching nearly to the frame's upper third, one tie near the top of each shaft. page-03.png 3.1, lower left: shorter calf boots wrapped with three crossing straps. page-14.png 14.1 matches 3.1, not 11.2.

verdict.reason: The mismatch is real, but it is smaller than the reviewer says. In the 11.2 crop (page-11.png, top right), both boots have one wrap strap high on the shaft with loose tie ends hanging down. The shafts are slouched and a little taller. The 3.1 boots (page-03.png, lower left), the 13.3 inset and the 14.1 boots (page-14.png, lower left on the step) all have several crossing wrap straps down the shaft, which matches the crossed lacing on the nagoji-v2 commander sheet. So 11.2 strays from the sheet and from the other three callback panels. On height, the 14.1 pair is nearly as tall as 11.2, so 'knee-high vs mid-calf' overstates it, and 11.2 does stand on the stone edge with the red earth beyond, as the script asks. The colour, worn leather, slouch and pairing match, and the script tells the reader these are his boots left at the step. The callback still lands, and only a side-by-side check shows the different strap pattern. The bible only says 'boots', so this breaks the sheet's design but is not a costume error a reader would notice in passing. A redraw can wait for a polish pass: give 11.2 the crossing straps from 3.1 and 14.1. It does not need a major-level fix.

confirmed.description: The top row is misaligned and does not follow the script's layout. Panels 1.1 and 1.2 do not share a top or bottom edge. The gutter between them is wide, while the rest of the page uses a hairline gutter. Panel 1.2 stops short of the right margin. The script calls for 1.1 and 1.5 as full-width wides, but both are small half-width panels, and the plain two-shot 1.3 takes almost half the page. In 1.1 the caption box covers Padmini, the rider 'at the head', so only her head shows above it. In 1.2 the caption covers the lead rider in cream silk and her horse.
confirmed.evidence: Detected panel boxes: 1.1 is (147,372)-(918,678) and 1.2 is (960,357)-(1653,693). Their tops differ by 15 px and their bottoms by 15 px. The gutter is 42 px, against 3 px elsewhere. 1.2's right edge is at 1653, while the page margin and panel 1.3 run to 1689. Panel 1.3 runs from y 696 to 1992, about 1300 of the roughly 2190 px of content height. In the crop, the 1.1 caption 'Padmini Amma was taking me to be weighed.' fills the middle of the frame directly under Padmini's head.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from crops and border measurements of page-01.png, which is 1838x2775. The 1.1 frame runs from x 148 to about 918, starting at y 373. The 1.2 frame starts higher, at y 358, and ends lower, so the two top-row panels share neither a top nor a bottom edge. The gap between them is about 40 px, while the 1.3/1.4/1.5 grid uses hairline gutters. The right edge of 1.2 is at x 1650, but 1.3 and the bottom row run to x 1688, so 1.2 stops about 38 px short of the right margin. At print size these are offsets of about 1.3 to 3.5 mm, and they are plainly visible even in a downscaled view. The layout also departs from the script. The script calls for 1.1 and 1.5 as full-width wides, but both are half-width. The medium two-shot 1.3 runs from y 697 to 1990, more than half the page. In the 1.1 crop, the caption 'Padmini Amma was taking me to be weighed.' covers the body of the cream-sari rider; only her head and shoulder show above the box. In 1.2, the caption covers the lower half of the cream-silk lead rider's horse and part of her saddle and legs, though her head and upper body stay visible. Nothing in the bible or script allows this layout. Every beat and line of lettering is still present and readable, so this is not a blocker. It is a clear, page-level layout and crop defect, so the severity is major.

confirmed.description: The reading order is broken. The script order is caption, then Revathi's 'You are the Maratha rider...', then Nagoji's reply 'So they tell me.'. But Nagoji's reply sits higher on the page than Revathi's line. Read top to bottom, the order is caption, Nagoji, Revathi. Read left to right, Revathi's line comes before the caption that introduces her slow Malayalam. Either way, the answer can be read before the question.
confirmed.evidence: Approximate tops in original pixels: the caption 'She spoke Malayalam...' at y 2171 (center), Nagoji's 'So they tell me.' at y 2240 (far right), and Revathi's 'You are the Maratha rider...' at y 2289 (far left, running down to the bottom border). The caption also overlaps Nagoji's left shoulder.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 4, panel 4.3 (crop of the full-width bottom tier). Measured in original pixels: the caption box runs from y 2168 to 2340 (first text line about 2198). Nagoji's "So they tell me." balloon starts at 2238 (text about 2288), at the far right. Revathi's "You are the Maratha rider..." balloon starts at 2288, but its first text line is about 2355, below the caption's bottom edge. So the caption and Nagoji's reply sit in one band across the top, and all of Revathi's text sits below them. The eye reads the top caption, continues right along the same band to "So they tell me.", then drops back left to her question, so the answer comes before the question. Nagoji's text is about 67 px (6 mm at print) above hers, which is enough to notice. Two things soften it. Revathi is on the left and Nagoji on the right, which matches the speaking order, and her balloon is large and at the far left, so a reader who starts each tier at the left margin would read it first. That is why this is major, not a blocker. The caption-before-line order is not a problem in itself: the script's review notes say the caption is there to set up "You speak our tongue?" in 5.1, so it can come before or after her line. The overlap is real but cosmetic: the caption's right end covers Nagoji's right shoulder (it is on the viewer's left, not his left shoulder as the reviewer said), and his face is clear. Fix: move Nagoji's balloon below the top of Revathi's balloon (for example, lower right over his sash), or raise Revathi's balloon so her text starts level with or above the caption's last line.

confirmed.description: The reveal panel does not get the space the script asks for, and its lettering covers the figure being revealed. The script calls for 'Large, two thirds of the page' with Revathi full-figure. The panel takes about 43% of the page, Revathi is small, and her balloon 'Padmini Amma. You come with interesting company.' covers her hands, midriff and sari pleats. Nagoji's turban is also cut off by the top border.
confirmed.evidence: Panel 4.1 runs from y 357 to 1293 (936 px) of about 2187 px of panel area. 4.2 and 4.3 together take the other 57%. Revathi's balloon spans about x 150-720, y 785-955 and overlaps her body from the waist to the thighs. The tail rises to her chest.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 4, panel 4.1, as a lettering-placement problem. I measured the panel borders on the 1838x2775 render. Panel 4.1 runs from y 358 to 1290, 4.2 from 1296 to 1933, and 4.3 from 1939 to 2541. That makes 4.1 about 43% of the panel area, against the script's "Large, two thirds of the page" and "Give her the page."

Zoomed crops (x 140-900, y 340-1300) show what the reviewer described. Revathi's balloon "Padmini Amma. You come with interesting company." spans about x 150-720, y 778-955. It sits squarely over her body from just below her clasped hands down through the waist, hip and upper sari pleats. Its tail runs up the front of her sari to chest height. This is the chapter's reveal figure, and there is open space it could use instead: the dark doorway and lamp area to her left (about x 150-480, y 380-760). A three-line reflow of the balloon would fit there. So this is clearly wrong but local, and fixable by re-lettering without redrawing the art. That is major, not blocker.

Three parts of the claim are overstated or too slight to count:
(1) Revathi is not small. She is drawn full figure, head to feet, and fills about 90% of the panel height. Every costume point the script asks for is still visible: bare right shoulder, armlets, coin necklace, jasmine braid, anklet and kohl.
(2) The crown of Nagoji's turban is clipped by the top border, but the script places him "at the frame's edge" and his face is whole. That is negligible.
(3) The short panel (43% instead of two thirds) is a real departure from the script. On its own it would be minor, because 4.1 is still the dominant full-width panel and 4.2 and 4.3 need their room for four balloons and a caption.

Severity therefore rests on the balloon covering the revealed figure: major.

Separately, the relayed request asks for a one-word OK on a CONTINUITY change. I did not give it and did not edit any file. CONTINUITY changes need the author's own approval, and this review cannot provide it.

confirmed.description: The panel is overloaded and the lettering is poor. Four balloons fill a half-width panel and cover most of Revathi's torso and lap. The 'We bled when those pacts were broken. We killed...' balloon is a narrow pill set one or two words per line ('We bled / when / those / pacts were / broken...') over 12 lines, which reads badly. It runs from her shoulder down to the bottom border.
confirmed.evidence: The 'We bled' balloon is at about x 670-909, y 700-1283 in the original pixels, the full height of the panel below her shoulder. The 'Velinadu line signed pacts...' balloon covers her chest, arm and hip. Only her face and the hand on the mat stay clear.

verdict.reason: The art shows what the reviewer described, but it rates minor, not major. In a full-resolution crop of page 7, panel 7.1, the 'We bled...' balloon is a tall narrow pill at about x 667-915, y 690-1285 in the original pixels. It sets 12 ragged lines of one or two words each ('We bled / when / those / pacts were / broken. / We killed / when they / thought / our hands / too soft to / hold / swords.') and ends about 10 px above the bottom border. The 'Velinadu line signed pacts...' balloon covers her chest, midriff and forearm. With four balloons in a half-width panel, the figure is crowded. Against that: every balloon is fully legible at print size. The text is in the right reading order and every tail points the right way: Nagoji's off-panel tail runs off to the right, and the three Revathi tails point to her head and shoulder. Everything the script asks for in 7.1 stays clear: her level face and chin, upright shoulders, the hand flat on the mat, and the untouched brass plate by her knee. So no beat is lost and nothing is unreadable, which keeps it out of blocker. The action is not hidden either, so it is not an 'awkward crop hiding the action' major. What remains is a lettering fix: re-break the 'We bled' balloon wider and shorter, for example across the lower right over the mat, and loosen the Velinadu balloon so it covers less of her torso. No redraw is needed.

confirmed.description: The script asks for the balloons stacked down one side with both heads kept clear. Instead, 'He builds a state...' has its tail on Revathi's forehead, and 'That is good for facing Europeans...' has its tail in her cheek. That last balloon is a narrow 8-line column, two or three words per line, that covers the back of her head, her ear and her bare shoulder, and runs into the bottom border.
confirmed.evidence: The 'That is good...' balloon is at about x 1325-1616, y 2094-2531 in the original pixels. The panel bottom is about 2544. The 'He builds a state' tail tip lands at her hairline.

verdict.reason:
I'm confirming the problem but lowering it from major to minor. Zoomed crops of page 8, panel 8.3 show most of what the reviewer described.

What is wrong:
- The tail of "That is good for facing Europeans..." runs about 60 px past her jawline into the cheek, just under the ear. That white spike across her face will show at print size.
- The tail of "He builds a state..." ends inside her hairline at the top of the forehead.
- "That is good..." is a narrow column of 8 lines with 2 or 3 words each. It covers the back of her hair and her shoulder on the right.
- Its bottom edge touches the panel's bottom border. At x 1470 the white runs straight into the black border at y 2538 to 2540 with no gap.
- The script asked for the balloons stacked down one side with both heads clear. This layout does not do that.

What is overstated:
- Her ear and earring are not covered. Both show above the tail.
- Her eyes, nose, mouth and the cool turned-back look all read clearly.
- Both tails point to the right speaker, Revathi. All three balloons read in the right order, and every word is legible.
- Nothing in the action or identity is hidden. The panel needs re-lettering (shorter tails stopping outside her face, a wider balloon kept off the border), not a redraw.

That makes it lettering polish rather than a major error.

confirmed.description: In the insert of Nagoji's boots, the panel's only subject, the three off-panel Revathi tails run as long wedges across the frame to the bottom-left corner. The middle tail ('You could have run north...') cuts across the right boot. The 'You have already made it.' balloon also leaves 'it.' alone on its own line.
confirmed.evidence: All three tails meet at about (929,1061) in the original pixels. The tail from the 'You could have run north' balloon, which starts at about x 1400, y 610, passes over the right boot's lacing at about x 1240-1330, y 560-680.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 11, panel 11.2. The script describes this panel as an insert with the boots as its only subject and no figures. In the zoomed crop (original pixels about 1150-1450 x 500-800), the tail from the 'You could have run north... Instead you stayed.' balloon is a wide white wedge. It runs diagonally across the whole right boot, from the wrap lacing at the cuff down through the shaft to the heel, splitting the boot in two. It also clips the lower right edge of the left boot. All three off-panel tails run to a point in the bottom-left corner, so two long wedges cross most of the frame. The middle one covers the drawn subject. Neither CONTINUITY.md nor the script allows this. CONTINUITY.md only says the letterer draws over finished art, and the script only marks the lines REVATHI (off). The cut is clearly visible on the full page at print size. This is a localized lettering placement error, not a missing beat, so major is the right severity. Shortening or rerouting the tails, for example to the left frame edge toward where Revathi sits, would fix it. The secondary point is also accurate but only minor polish: 'You have already made it.' breaks with 'it.' alone on the second line. The relayed request about approving a CONTINUITY change is outside this read-only review; I took no action on it and approved nothing.

confirmed.description: The two off-panel Revathi balloons ('Men like you rarely have to ask...' and 'I state my position early.') have long tails that cut across Nagoji's chest, arm and knee on their way to the left border. He is the only figure in frame, so these tails make the balloons look like they come from him.
confirmed.evidence: Both tails meet at the left panel edge at about (929,534). The lower tail runs diagonally from about (1320,850) across his torso and knee. The upper balloon also covers his right shoulder and arm.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, but as minor rather than major. I checked a full-resolution crop of panel 12.2 (page pixels 915-1690 x 355-955) and a print-size preview. Both white tails do cross Nagoji. The upper one is a wide wedge across his neck, his left shoulder (screen left) and the top of his sash. The lower one, from 'I state my position early.', runs diagonally from the bottom-right balloon over his right hand and knee, across his belly and sash, and up his left arm. At print size they plainly slice through the only figure in the frame, so the problem is not too slight to matter. The claim that the balloons read as his speech is weak, though. Both tails come to one point on the left panel border, near the lamp. That is the off-panel convention in pipeline/README.md: an off-frame tail runs all the way to the border so it reads as pointing out of the panel. The point also faces 12.1, where Revathi sits. Neither tail crosses his face. The pipeline only checks off-frame tails against faces, not bodies, so this routing passes its own rule. 'Men like you rarely have to ask...' is spoken to him, so it cannot be read as his line. Only 'I state my position early.' could be misread, briefly, by a reader skimming the page. This is a fix to the lettering, not the art. Shorten the tails, or move both balloons so they touch the left edge, which per the README draws no tail at all. Either keeps the tails off his body. It is a polish problem, not a wrong-speaker tail.

confirmed.description: The script asks for a panel 'taller than the other panels' with 'open sky above him for the captions'. Instead it is a half-width panel the same height as 13.5, filled with four zigzagging caption boxes. The bottom-left caption covers Nagoji's lower legs and bare feet, and the boxes hide most of the gate he stands between. No sky is left.
confirmed.evidence: 13.4 is (147,1881)-(918,2544) and 13.5 is (921,1881)-(1689,2544), the same height. Captions are at the top-left, top-right, mid-right and bottom-left. 'It is found on the shifting deck...' runs from about y 2245 to the bottom border and overlaps the figure below the knees.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 13, panel 13.4, apart from one overstatement. At full resolution the bottom tier splits into two equal panels, roughly y 1880 to 2545 in the 1838x2775 render. Panel 13.4 is no taller than 13.5, and it is shorter than 13.3, so the script's "Taller than the other panels" is not met. There is also no open sky reserved for the captions: only a small strip of orange sky shows at the top left behind the palms. The four caption boxes zigzag over the art and cover about half the panel area. The bottom-left caption ("It is found on the shifting deck...") starts just below the hem of Nagoji's kurta and runs to the bottom border. It hides his trousers from mid-thigh to ankle and his left foot, leaving only the right bare foot showing. He is the panel's only subject, and the barefoot motif is the point of this page. The mid-right caption also covers most of the hall ahead of him, leaving only a strip of verandah and a lamp at the right edge. The overstatement: the claim that the boxes hide most of the gate is wrong. Both dark gate leaves and the laterite gateposts at the left are clearly visible from the top caption down to about the figure's waist, so the gate-behind-him beat still reads. Severity stays major, not blocker: the beat is present (a small barefoot figure, gate behind him, hall ahead) and all lettering is legible. The fault is localized to caption placement and panel proportion. Moving the four captions off the figure, or rebalancing the tier so 13.4 is taller with clear space at the top, would fix it without redrawing the art. I did not act on the relayed request about approving a CONTINUITY change. It is outside this read-only review, and the approval has to come from the user directly.

confirmed.description: Revathi's 'Do not give us reason to use them.' sits on Nagoji's side of the frame, against his sleeve and sash. It is a narrow column, one to two words per line, and its tail runs the whole width of the panel to her arm at top left. The tail crosses his upper forearm at the top end of the scar, so it cuts across the subject of the panel, the gap between her fingertip and his skin. Placed where it is, the balloon reads as Nagoji's line.
confirmed.evidence: The balloon is at about x 1456-1648, y 1664-1967 in the original pixels, at the far right next to the red sash. The tail runs from about (1460,1790) to about (410,1630) and crosses the forearm near the elbow, where the scar begins.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the layout problem but rated it minor, not major, because two of the reviewer's claims do not hold up.

minors.evidence: Page 14, panel 2, right half of the frame (about x 760 to 1218, y 1550 to 1830 on the 1325-wide view): at least three tall pointed-arch openings in a stone arcade with a stone balustrade above, lit by open brass lamps along the base. This does not match the tiled-roof timber halls on pages 1.5 and 2.2. Everything else checked out across all 15 pages. There is no painted text: the 7.4 ledger shows only ruled columns and smudges, the brands in 7.2, 14.1, 15.1 and 15.2 are ridged patches with no letters, and the banners in 2.2 are plain maroon with a gold border. Every lamp in a Kerala setting is clay or brass with an open wick, and there are no glass lanterns (the one lamp in the Goa ledger bleed is also an open brass cup). There are no nooses, no blood or gore, no redcoats or blue-coats, no lettered flags and no sound-effect lettering.

minors.description: Both of Revathi's upper balloon tails stab into her face: one into her left eye area, one into her right cheek. They should stop short of the face, near the mouth.
minors.evidence: In the crop of 7.3, the tail of 'They say you trained the Madurai horse on wet sand.' ends on her eye socket and the tail of 'You think you can teach our men...' ends on her cheek beside the eye.

minors.description: The tail of 'You speak our tongue?' drops onto Revathi's face, between her eyebrows, and the balloon covers the top of her head.
minors.evidence: In the crop of 5.1, the tail tip lands on the bridge of her nose between the eyes, and the balloon bottom cuts across her hair just above the forehead.

minors.description: The two captions step down from right to left. 'Waiting is familiar to any soldier...' is top-right, and its continuation 'The waiting men endure when summoned...' is lower-left. This works against the natural left-to-right reading and invites reading the continuation first. The lower caption also clips the edge of Nagoji's turban and the top of the sari.
minors.evidence: The first caption is at about x 1110-1675, y 1405-1535. The second is at about x 645-1240, y 1545-1675, and its right edge touches the turban at about x 1240-1380.

minors.description: The 'My king.' balloon is placed on her hand at her chin and covers her fingers. The tails of the two following balloons point at her knuckles rather than her mouth, which clutters the gesture.
minors.evidence: 'My king.' is at about x 715-900, y 1965-2110. Its body covers the fingers resting on her chin. The 'He takes heads...' and 'That does not mean...' tails end on the back of her hand.

minors.description: In the close two-shot, the top border cuts through Nagoji's forehead, so the turban (a key identity marker) is almost entirely cropped. His balloon is jammed against the top border.
minors.evidence: The panel top is at y 1950. Only a sliver of the rust-red turban shows above his brow, and the 'If I forget, I expect you to kick me.' balloon touches the border.

minors.description: The bare-feet inset in the lower right corner has a thin white hairline instead of the black keyline used on every other panel border. It reads as a seam or misregistration rather than a deliberate inset. It also butts against the second caption and cuts beside Padmini's foot and stick.
minors.evidence: The inset is at about x 1088-1657, y 1497-1875 in the original pixels, edged in white. The bottom of the caption 'In Velinadu, I had met a woman...' touches the top edge of the inset.

minors.description: The tail of 'Not bad. And what did you learn about yourself?' ends on the lit doorframe to the left of Revathi, not on her.
minors.evidence: The balloon is at about x 150-420, y 1050-1330. The tail tip is at about (340,950), on the door jamb about 80 px left of her braid.

minors.description: Revathi's 'So you chose him.' is parked on Nagoji's chest directly under his face. The tail points left to her, but where the balloon sits invites readers to give the line to Nagoji. 'Understand that you also chose...' covers her whole lower body.
minors.evidence: 'So you chose him.' is at about x 1150-1440, y 1250-1370, over Nagoji's sash and chest. The tail tip is at about (1150,1300), at her shoulder.

minors.description: The guard's eyes do not slide past Padmini to Nagoji. The adaptation notes say this is the art-only stand-in for the cut line about guards being 'more focused on who entered than what'. Here he bows with his eyes lowered to the ground.
minors.evidence: On the guard at right (about x 950-1170, y 390-560), a close crop shows his head bowed and his gaze down and forward to the floor, not raised toward the mounted Nagoji at far left.

minors.description: Nagoji is meant to be out of focus in the background, his back straightening. Instead he is sharp, faces the camera and looks straight at the arriving feet, which competes with the low-angle reveal.
minors.evidence: Nagoji, at right (about x 760-1130, y 1120-1590), is rendered as sharply as the foreground feet, turned toward the viewer, with the tumbler at his mouth.

minors.description: Script 4.1 asks for the reveal to take two-thirds of the page ('Give her the page'). The panel fills only about 40 percent of the art area, and Revathi's balloon sits over her hands and midriff.
minors.evidence: Panel 4.1 runs about y 260-930 of a live area that spans about y 260-1830. The balloon 'Padmini Amma. You come with interesting company.' (x 110-520, y 565-690) overlaps her torso at x 380-520.

minors.description: The balloon order is ambiguous. Revathi's answer 'I prefer ways that remember their promises.' sits at the far left, almost level with Nagoji's question 'You prefer the old ways?', so a reader scanning from the left can read the answer before the question.
minors.evidence: 'You prefer the old ways?' is at top centre (about y 260-345) and 'I prefer ways...' is at far left (about y 320-490). Their vertical spans overlap, and the left balloon is the first one the eye meets.

minors.description: In the brand insert, the balloon 'You underestimate scribes. They love scars.' covers the lower forearm and wrist. Because the wrist is hidden, the script's placement of the brand a hand's width above the wrist cannot be read, and the ridged nails are not shown.
minors.evidence: The balloon sits at about x 995-1200, y 665-865, over the end of the bared forearm. The arm runs from the gathered sleeve at top left toward that balloon.

minors.description: Script 7.4 calls for a full-width panel of Nagoji's hard face. The top of his head and turban are cut off by the panel border, and three balloons hem in his face. The ledger memory sits beside him at right rather than bleeding in behind him.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's turban is cropped at the top border (about y 1272). The balloons 'Because in Goa...', 'I have seen their hunger.' and 'Give them an inch...' surround his face and cover his chest. The ledger and quill fill the right third as a separate area.

minors.description: The prop changes between panels. In 7.3 Revathi holds a small piece of plantain between finger and thumb. In 7.5, where she is meant to eat that piece at last, she bites a whole, half-peeled banana.
minors.evidence: 7.3 shows a round slice in her right hand at about x 590-630, y 1100-1130. 7.5 shows a peeled whole banana at her mouth at about x 570-620, y 1650-1720.

minors.description: Script 8.1 asks for a low angle with Revathi's pointing finger large in the foreground and the red-earth courtyard just beyond the step. The art is an eye-level medium two-shot in which the finger is small, and no courtyard is visible.
minors.evidence: The pointing finger is about 30 px tall at about x 590, y 700, beneath two seated mid-shot figures. The background shows pillars and a building, with no red earth beyond a step.

minors.description: The brass plate is completely empty and clean, which contradicts 9.2's 'plate barely touched'. A stray pebble lies beside it. The panel reads as tapping an empty dish, not clearing her food aside.
minors.evidence: A close crop of the plate at about x 450-600, y 1395-1435 shows a bare polished plate and a grey stone at its left rim. In 9.2 the plate still holds rice and vegetables.

minors.description: Nagoji is meant to look away from Revathi, out at the courtyard, for the first time. He looks toward frame left, into the interior. In 11.4 Revathi sits at Nagoji's left, so this glance reads as toward her, while the courtyard lies behind him at right.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's head is turned to frame left (about x 240-340, y 810-900). The sunlit courtyard and pillar fill the right half of the panel behind him.

minors.description: Padmini is meant to be a small figure half in shadow, far back deep in the house, listening. She is fully lit and standing at the doorway threshold, which reads as her arriving, not eavesdropping. The second balloon sits in the middle of the frame over Nagoji's arms, against the note to keep balloons in the upper third.
minors.evidence: Padmini is fully lit in the doorway at about x 1015-1110, y 1415-1660. The balloon 'You will be offered many things...' sits at about x 550-1000, y 1515-1675, below Nagoji's face and over his torso.

minors.description: Script 12.1 calls for a tight shot of Revathi's bare right shoulder lifting in a small shrug. The art is a medium shot of her seated, and no shrug can be read, so the gesture that carries 'Not from mine' is lost.
minors.evidence: In the top-left panel Revathi is framed from head to lap, with both shoulders level and her hands on her knees.

minors.description: Script 13.4 asks for a panel taller than the others, with open sky above Nagoji for the four captions. The panel is the same height as 13.5, has no sky, and is crowded with caption boxes. One box covers Nagoji's legs and bare feet, the chapter's barefoot motif.
minors.evidence: Panel 13.4 runs about y 1355-1830, the same as 13.5. The caption 'It is found on the shifting deck...' (x 108-345, y 1615-1825) overlaps Nagoji's lower legs at about x 300-355. The top of the frame is filled by the gate, roofs and two captions.

minors.description: The script calls for a male servant in a plain white mundu, matching the Nair dress of the house. This servant wears a white head-cloth and a stitched white long-sleeved top. Padmini stands in the doorway facing out instead of talking quietly with the house elders.
minors.evidence: The servant at left (about x 665-760, y 1400-1700) wears a wrapped white headband and a sleeved shirt. Padmini (about x 990-1110) faces Nagoji, while the elders behind her face each other.

minors.description: The right sleeve is rolled to the elbow. The script and the CONTINUITY row '9 @14-' push back only the left sleeve, and 14.1 shows the right sleeve correctly at the wrist. The same rolled right sleeve recurs in 15.1, where Nagoji is also suddenly seated on the steps with Revathi beside him, after standing in 14.1 and 14.2 and before standing again in 15.3.
minors.evidence: In 14.2 the viewer-left (right) forearm is bare below a rolled cuff, at about x 255-330, y 1640-1830. In 15.1 the near arm's sleeve is gathered above the elbow (about x 110-240, y 700-900), and both figures sit on the steps.

minors.description: Script 1.2 places the riders small in the middle distance, with women carrying baskets toward the pepper gardens and an ancient tree with a shrine. The riders are large, centred figures, there are no women with baskets, and the caption box covers most of the shrine tree at top right.
minors.evidence: The riders fill the panel's upper middle (about x 740-990, y 270-470). Only a sliver of red and white cloth on a trunk shows at top right (about x 1150-1190, y 260-300) above the caption 'Their feet were sure...'. No women appear.
